papers.title: Rapid Charge Stability Diagram Generation from Device-level Modeling of Semiconductor Quantum Dots
papers.summary: Self-consistent Schrödinger-Poisson calculations are a powerful tool for predicting the behavior of layered semiconductor quantum dot devices. However, characterization of charge stability diagrams through fully simulated gate-voltage sweeps is computationally expensive. Combining a Multi-Domain Multi-Model (MDMM) approach with an automated tuning routine, we identify gate voltages associated with selected charge configurations. This small set of self-consistent simulations can be augmented with Full Configuration Interaction (FCI) energy calculations to extract charging energies, lever arms, and interdot Coulomb interactions to directly parameterize a Hubbard model for rapid charge stability diagram generation. For an Intel Tunnel Falls Si/SiGe device, we demonstrate the Hubbard model's ability to reproduce charge stability diagrams at a fraction of the computational cost in comparison to voltage bias sweeps. We further compare the simulated diagrams to experimental data and demonstrate qualitative agreement. Our result represents a step towards predictive digital twin models for semiconductor quantum dot devices. Finally, we apply this workflow towards lever arm engineering in a second device, demonstrating that the method extends to multiple architectures.

papers.title: Design of DC gate electric field redistribution under high drain voltage for high linearity, wide gain control range, and low C off in GaN dual-mode integrated devices
papers.summary: In this work, we propose and demonstrate a technique for optimizing linearity and off-state capacitance (Coff) in dual-mode integrated gallium nitride high-electron-mobility transistors with direct current (DC) gate bias control. In the dual-mode integrated high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT), the large-resistance bias gate near the drain serves as a modulator for transconductance (gm) and off-state capacitance. It is shown that, in power amplifier mode, adjusting the DC gate bias redistributes the electric field, effectively reduces the peak field between the gate and drain, delays carrier velocity saturation, and mitigates self-heating effects, thereby significantly improving gm under high drain voltage. Measurements demonstrate that by optimizing the DC gate bias, both the output third-order intercept point (OIP3) and the gain of the dual-mode integrated HEMT are markedly enhanced. At 8 GHz and Vd = 50 V, increasing the DC gate bias from −2 to 28 V yields a tunable range of 12.1 dB and an OIP3 of 38.6 dBm. In switching mode, applying a negative DC gate bias introduces a series capacitance and reduces the radio frequency gate capacitance formed by the two-dimensional electron gas, resulting in an ultralow Coff of approximately 5 fF/mm. More importantly, this approach provides a new design degree of freedom: simply varying the DC level of the gate bias enables continuous tuning of the device's linearity, gain, and isolation.

papers.title: Experimental Investigation of Gate-Switching Instability in SiC MOSFETs Under Mission-Profile-Related Non-Monotonic Stress
papers.summary: In high-power-density and efficient power electronic systems, SiC MOSFETs are increasingly used for their superior performance. However, their gate oxide/semiconductor interface remains challenging, and additional degradation mechanisms, such as gate-switching instability (GSI), occur. Extensive monotonic-stress studies have shown that negative gate-source voltage peaks dominate GSI-related degradation, even when occurring only during undershoots. Consequently, degradation depends on the mission profile because gate-voltage undershoot varies with gate resistance, gate-loop inductance, and drain current. However, the resulting non-monotonic GSI-related degradation has not been thoroughly investigated. This letter demonstrates that accounting for gate undershoots is crucial for estimating degradation over the component’s lifetime, as the pre-existing degradation level strongly influences further degradation. This behavior applies to both GSI-related defect activation and deactivation. Furthermore, defect deactivation is highly dependent on the positive gate-source voltage, and after a stress change, even 600 mV of degradation recovers to the degradation obtained under monotonic stress at the same gate-source voltage within ${2}\!\cdot\!{10}^{{11}}$ switching cycles. Additionally, GSI-related defect activation strongly depends on the degradation level, and consequently, mission-profile-related gate-voltage undershoots must be considered, even if they occur only during 5% of the mission profile.

papers.title: Multi-Channel AlScN/GaN RF HEMTs Grown by Metal-Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition
papers.summary: We demonstrate multi-channel AlScN/GaN high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) grown by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD). The five-channel structure exhibits a high electron mobility ( $\mu $ ) of 1030 cm 2 /V $\cdot $ s together with a high carrier concentration ( ${n} {_{\text {s}}}$ ) of ${3}.{58}\times {10} {^{{13}}}$ cm −2 . Devices with a gate length ( ${L} {_{\text {g}}}$ ) of 95 nm and a total gate width ( ${W} {_{\text {g}}}$ ) of ${2}\times {15}~\mu $ m were fabricated using a tri-gate architecture with varying fin widths. The 300 nm fin width device achieves a current density of 4.2 A/mm with improved linearity, while reducing the fin width to 75 nm enhances electrostatic control over all channels and yields ${f} {_{\text {T}}}$ / ${f} {_{\text {MAX}}}$ of 70/163 GHz. The passivated devices retain a stable I ${}_{\text {D,max}}$ under repeated measurements and an off-state breakdown of 18.5 V at ${\text L}_{\text {GD}} =400$ nm. These results highlight the promise of MOCVD-grown AlScN/GaN multi-channel HEMTs for RF applications, with strong DC and small-signal RF characteristics, motivating further study of their large-signal performance for mm-wave operation.

papers.title: Regrowth-Free Ex-Situ Mg-Diffused GaN-Based HBTs With High Gain of ~200
papers.summary: We demonstrate a high-gain, regrowth-free AlGaN/(In)GaN heterojunction bipolar transistor (HBT) enabled by ex-situ thermal annealing of a patterned metallic magnesium (Mg) film on plasma-damaged p-GaN base layers. Plasma etching of the base region typically introduces surface defects that increase surface recombination and degrade base transport. The proposed Mg/GaN annealing process induces shallow diffusion of a high-concentration Mg acceptor profile near the base surface, mitigating plasma-induced damage without epitaxial regrowth. Circular transfer length method (CTLM) confirms good ohmic contact with linear $I$ – $V$ characteristics and a low specific contact resistivity of $2.38\times 10^{-{5}} \Omega \cdot $ cm 2 . The suppression of base surface recombination reduces the base current, resulting in more than a fourfold increase in the dc current gain $\beta $ from 42 to 197 and the differential gain ${h}_{\text {fe}}$ from 50 to 240, despite the relatively large emitter size of $40\times 40~\mu $ m 2 . In addition, the differential specific on-resistance ${R}_{\text {on,sp}}$ decreases from 32.0 m $\Omega \cdot $ cm 2 to 1.35 m $\Omega \cdot $ cm 2 after the Mg annealing process. These results highlight the strong potential of ex-situ Mg diffusion as a scalable strategy for enhancing the performance of GaN-based HBTs.

papers.title: Coherent phononic frequency combs in ferroelectric CMOS oxides
papers.summary: Modern electronic systems require tens of clock and carrier frequencies, each synthesized by a dedicated phase-locked loop from a shared reference, imposing routing, power and synchronization burdens that grow with every domain. Optical frequency combs solved this problem in photonics, whereas electronics has lacked an equivalent source in its native radiofrequency domain. Here we report broadband phononic frequency combs in ferroelectric hafnia-zirconia nanoelectromechanical resonators built from complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) oxides. Lithographically defined detuning of a 2:1 internal resonance selects the generation mechanism: two-tone-seeded wave mixing yields more than 170 lines distributed over two octaves, with mutual coherence verified for representative pump and generated lines, whereas an autonomous Hopf route yields hierarchical combs of more than 200 lines through torus and period-doubling dynamics, in agreement with slow-flow bifurcation theory. Geometric scaling extends comb generation across 0.44 GHz to 2.1 GHz. Heterodyne measurements, analyzed using the modified Allan deviation (MDEV), establish a two-timescale law. The mechanism governs short-term stability: seeded combs inherit the white-phase-noise scaling of their pumps, whereas autonomous combs acquire the phase diffusion of a free-running oscillator, with the one-second MDEV increasing from 1e-11 to 1e-8. The material governs long-term stability: in air and without active thermal control, the temperature-compensated stack suppresses the random-walk drift that dominates uncompensated resonators. These results establish mechanism- and material-level design rules for operating a single resonator as chip-scale frequency infrastructure, from multi-clock generation to radiofrequency parallel processing.

papers.title: GaN-on-Si JBS Diode Using Drive-In Diffusion to Shield p-GaN Regrowth Interface and Achieving a Breakdown Voltage Beyond 1 kV
papers.summary: This letter reports a GaN-on-Si junction barrier Schottky (JBS) diode with regrown p-GaN wells. To address the notorious Si impurities and defects at the regrowth interface, a post-regrowth drive-in diffusion technique is developed, which pushes the PN junction face beyond the regrowth interface. As a result, the electric field peak in the OFF-state is shifted away from the regrowth interface. The reference JBS diodes (without drive-in diffusion) present a low breakdown voltage ( BV ) of ~20 V irrespective of the p-well spacing ${W}_{\text {n}}$ , indicating that the excessive leakage current originates from the regrown p-well region rather than the Schottky junction. The JBS diodes with drive-in diffusion achieve BV s of 716 V for ${W}_{\text {n}} = 3~\mu $ m and 1021 V for ${W}_{\text {n}} = 2~\mu $ m. This work demonstrates that drive-in diffusion is a promising approach for realizing regrowth-based JBS diodes in GaN.

papers.title: Semi-On State Hole Generation in GaN HEMTs: Experimental Evidence and TCAD Modeling
papers.summary: We explore the physical mechanisms responsible for hole generation in GaN HEMTs in the semi-on state by experimentally investigating dependence of gate-collected hole current on ${V}_{\text {DS}}$ , ${V}_{\textit {GS}}$ and temperature. Three key observations contradict conventional impact ionization: the hole current 1) saturates at high electric fields; 2) exhibits a positive temperature dependence; and 3) has a low trigger voltage of $\mathbf {V}_{\text {DS}}={2}.{7} {V}$ at 5 K, which is significantly below the GaN bandgap energy. We therefore propose trap-assisted hole generation as the underlying mechanism and implement a corresponding behavioral model in TCAD. TCAD simulations accurately reproduce the observed dependencies of hole generation on ${V}_{\text {DS}}$ , ${V}_{\textit {GS}}$ and temperature.
